title: What Did Ofsted Want Schools to Improve in 2023-2024? e-in-2023-2024/
author: Peter Foster
summary: Peter Foster reads roughly 70 Ofsted inspection reports from 2023-2024, focused specifically on the 'areas for improvement' sections, and summarises the recurring themes by grade band. Across Good-rated primary schools, curriculum (especially foundation subjects), leadership of curriculum implementation, checking for understanding, and reading (particularly phonics) dominate. In Good-rated secondary schools, checking for understanding is the single most common theme, with curriculum, behaviour, and attendance following; Foster notes behaviour and attendance both feature far more prominently than in his equivalent 2022 reading. Requires Improvement schools show the same issues at greater intensity, with attendance and behaviour more pronounced still, and Inadequate-rated schools typically show safeguarding or unsafe-behaviour concerns. Foster is careful to frame the exercise as observational rather than rigorous research, and explicitly cautions against treating the list as a roadmap to school improvement, since Ofsted reports rarely explain how to fix what they flag. He closes with open questions about how a new Chief Inspector might shift these emphases and whether the current focus on checking for understanding and rising attendance/behaviour concerns reflect lasting or temporary conditions.
points: Foster's single strongest finding across both primary and secondary Good-rated schools is checking for understanding, which topped the list of improvement areas in a way it hadn't as clearly in his 2022 reading.

He flags that behaviour and attendance concerns have become markedly more prominent in Good-rated secondary reports since his 2022 read, calling out increased mentions of persistent absence among disadvantaged pupils specifically.
He explicitly disclaims the exercise as non-academic research (roughly 70 reports, not a systematic sample) and warns readers not to treat Ofsted's flagged areas as a genuine roadmap to improvement.

He notes Inadequate-rated schools cluster around a different category of concern entirely, safeguarding and unsafe behaviour, rather than the curriculum/assessment issues dominating Good and Requires Improvement bands.
quotes: My main aim was to better understand what schools are asked to improve by Ofsted.
I’ve read just over 70 Ofsted reports, with about half primary and half secondary. This is not academic research.
Check for understanding. The most common area for development on the implementation of the curriculum was the need for more (or the absence of) checking for understanding.
Attendance and behaviour have become more prominent in Good reports since 2022 as teachers working in schools could have told you.
Schools receiving this rating often have an issue with safeguarding (including training, processes or record keeping). Equally, behaviour may have become unsafe.
As I said at the start, this post isn’t written to give you a roadmap to school improvement. Ofsted reports don’t do that.
